newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end down, pull back from year highs.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end down, pull back from year highs.

text.p: All but two of the shares in the Paris bourse's CAC-40 index fell on Wednesday after a tumble on Wall Street knocked the market from the highest levels it has reached this year.
Traders said the market needed to breathe before resuming its advance with the goal of regaining the historic high of 2,360.98 points set in 1994.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 40.46 points or 1.72 percent at 2,308.65 -- a support level -- while the CAC-40 futures contract fell to 2,310 from 2,352 on Tuesday's close.
Volume was a solid 6.5 billion francs.
The next big support levels were seen at 2,280 and 2,240 points, and resistance was expected at 2,355, 2,368 and 2,375.

A trader at a French bank said some operators were caught wrong-footed by the 80-point drop on Wall Street on Tuesday and the 2,308 support could be breached on Thursday. But brokers said a correction may be healthy for the market after a straight-line run up since the end of August.

Lagardere shares fell seven percent to 145 francs after the government suspended plans to sell it the Thomson electronics group as part of its privatisation programme. Some 275 million francs worth of Lagardere stock traded.
Alcatel Alsthom, the rival bidder, saw its shares fall 3.18 percent to 460 francs on the fallout from the government's retreat from the controversial Thomson sale.
"The government was under so much pressure. It doesn't come as a surprise," said a broker. "It probably puts (Prime Minister) Juppe under more pressure."
